outcome: Through 11 October 2026 no event has settled or moved the infinitude question as written: no unconditional proof or disproof that infinitely many primes satisfy the congruence for a given base a has appeared since 26 January 2024. The in-window work is conditional on abc, concerns the complementary non-Wieferich primes, or treats number-field, Drinfeld-module or function-field analogues; several 2026 preprints use the Wieferich condition as an input without bearing on its infinitude. The statement as given (a^p − 1 ≡ 1 mod p²) and the live Wikipedia bullet (a^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p²) differ, and the two readings disagree at a = 1.
problem_asks: Parts, read from the statement given to this run: (1) a quantifier over every integer a > 0, with no bound on a; (2) for each such a, the claim that the set of primes p with a^p − 1 ≡ 1 (mod p²), equivalently a^p ≡ 2 (mod p²), is infinite. No restriction on p (for instance p not dividing a) and no range for p is stated. Each base a is a separate part, so a result for one a settles only that part. Wording check: the live Wikipedia list (fetched in 2026) has the bullet as 'For any given integer a > 0, are there infinitely many primes p such that a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p²)?' with footnote [185]. The January 2024 frozen text was not verified. Under the exponent p−1 reading, the parts are the same with the standard base-a Wieferich question: infinitely many primes p with a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p²). The two readings coincide for a = 2, since for odd p, 2^p ≡ 2 mod p² holds exactly when 2^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p². They differ elsewhere: for a = 1 the literal form has no solutions (0 ≢ 1 mod p²), so the set is empty, while the p−1 form holds for every prime. Research covered the statement as given and the standard p−1 form. No literature was found on the literal a^p ≡ 2 (mod p²) form as such.

events.what_happened: J. H. Silverman, 'Wieferich's criterion and the abc conjecture', J. Number Theory 30 (1988) 226–237. Assuming abc, for every nonzero base a (a ≠ ±1 in the stated form) there are at least a constant times log x primes p ≤ x with a^(p−1) ≢ 1 mod p². This concerns non-Wieferich primes. Read via secondary descriptions (Graves–Weiss 2025, Murty survey search summaries, Wikipedia); the paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Under abc, growth of at least order log x of base-a NON-Wieferich primes up to x, for every base a. Conditional on abc. Says nothing about whether base-a Wieferich primes are infinite.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The result is about the complementary set; the Wieferich set asked about is untouched.

checked_by.who: Journal of Number Theory (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for publication (journal listing, from secondary citations only)

events.doubts: A MathWorld entry for the abc conjecture says abc implies at least C ln x Wieferich primes ≤ x, which conflicts with Silverman's non-Wieferich statement as described by every other source found. The MathWorld wording appears to swap the two terms. Recorded as a source discrepancy in disputes.
events.direction: Cuts toward the complementary side: asserts many non-Wieferich primes (conditionally). Does not assert or deny infinitely many Wieferich primes.

events.what_happened: F. G. Dorais and D. Klyve, 'A Wieferich prime search up to 6.7 × 10^15', J. Integer Sequences 14 (2011), Article 11.9.2. Computation: no base-2 Wieferich primes other than 1093 and 3511 below 6.7 × 10^15. The paper says its methods could search for solutions of a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p²) for other small a but reports no outcomes for them.
events.delivers: A finite search: no further base-2 Wieferich primes below 6.7 × 10^15. Restricted to base 2. A finite check of a claim about infinitely many primes; it moves no infinitude statement.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. Base 2 only; no result for other bases; no infinitude claim.

checked_by.who: Journal of Integer Sequences (refereed); authors Dorais (University of Michigan) and Klyve (Central Washington University)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; authors are number theorists doing the computation

machine_checked.system: Custom search code by the authors (computer search, not a proof assistant)

events.directly_checkable: Anyone can test a^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p² for a given p with modular exponentiation; the stated result is the list of hits below the bound.
events.direction: Evidence of sparsity for base 2 (only 1093 and 3511 found below 6.7 × 10^15). Consistent with the open question; does not decide it.

events.what_happened: H. Graves and M. R. Murty, 'The abc conjecture and non-Wieferich primes in arithmetic progressions', J. Number Theory 133 (2013) 1809–1813. Assuming abc, for a ≥ 2 and k ≥ 2 there are at least order log x / log log x primes p ≤ x with a^(p−1) ≢ 1 mod p² and p ≡ 1 mod k. Read from secondary descriptions (search summaries, Graves–Weiss 2025); not opened.
events.delivers: Conditional on abc: growth of order log x / log log x of NON-Wieferich primes in progressions p ≡ 1 mod k. Complementary set; no statement about Wieferich primes being infinite.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (per AMS bibliography in search summary)

events.direction: Complementary (non-Wieferich) side, conditional on abc. Does not bear on infinitude of Wieferich primes.

events.what_happened: S. Kotyada and S. Muthukrishnan, 'Non-Wieferich primes in number fields and ABC conjecture', arXiv:1610.00488 (v1 3 Oct 2016; v2 10 Mar 2017), Czech. Math. J. 68 (2018) 445–453. For a number field K of class number one, assuming abc for number fields, there are infinitely many non-Wieferich primes with respect to certain units of O_K.
events.revisions: v1 3 Oct 2016; v2 10 Mar 2017 (minor revisions, to appear in Czech. Math. J.); journal 2018
events.delivers: Conditional on abc for number fields: infinitely many non-Wieferich primes relative to certain units in class-number-one fields. Number-field analogue on the complementary side. Not the integer base-a Wieferich question.
events.remains: All of problem_asks; the integer case is not addressed.
events.direction: Number-field analogue, complementary side, conditional on abc. Does not bear on infinitude of integer Wieferich primes.

events.what_happened: Yong-Gao Chen and Yu Ding, 'Non-Wieferich primes in arithmetic progressions', Proc. AMS 145 (2017) 1833–1836 (received 4 Nov 2015; published electronically 23 Jan 2017; corrigendum 2018). Assuming abc, improves the Graves–Murty bound to (log x / log log x)(log log log x)^M for any fixed M, for non-Wieferich primes p ≡ 1 mod k. Read from search summaries; the AMS page returned HTTP 403 on fetch.
events.revisions: Corrigendum published 2018 (Proc. AMS 146) on the introduction only
events.delivers: Conditional on abc: a sharper lower bound for NON-Wieferich primes in progressions. Complementary side only.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: Author attribution differs across sources: 'Yu Ding' here and 'Yuchen Ding' for the 2019 Comptes Rendus paper. Whether these are the same person was not established. Recorded in disputes.
events.direction: Complementary (non-Wieferich) side, conditional on abc.

events.what_happened: N. A. Carella, 'Results for Wieferich primes', arXiv:1712.08166 (v1 21 Dec 2017; v2 5 May 2018). Abstract: an asymptotic formula for the number of base-v Wieferich primes in a short interval [x, x+z], v ≥ 2; a prediction of a third base-2 Wieferich prime in [10^15, 10^40]; and the claim that 'the subset of nonWieferich primes has density 1', presented without a conditional or heuristic qualifier. Only the abstract page was read; the body was not.
events.revisions: v1 21 Dec 2017; v2 5 May 2018 (the version read is v2)
events.delivers: Per the abstract only: an asymptotic count of Wieferich primes in short intervals for fixed base v, and an unconditional density-1 claim for non-Wieferich primes. Even if the density-1 claim holds, a set of density zero can still be infinite, so it does not decide whether the Wieferich set is infinite. The short-interval formula is not stated as bearing on infinitude.
events.remains: Whether the Wieferich set is infinite, for any base a: not addressed in the abstract.
events.doubts: The density-1 claim contradicts the 2025 papers that state no unconditional result on non-Wieferich primes is known (Fellini–Murty 2025 and Graves–Weiss 2025 both say so, per secondary summaries; whether either cites Carella was not checked). Not resolved: the body was not read, so I cannot say whether the claim rests on a hypothesis. Searches found no refereed version and no public engagement. The short-interval formula is stated as exact, while the prediction in the same abstract is probabilistic.
events.direction: Abstract claims unconditional density 1 for non-Wieferich primes, which is the complementary side. Silent on whether Wieferich primes are infinite.

events.what_happened: M. Ram Murty, K. Srinivas and M. Subramani, 'Admissible primes and Euclidean quadratic fields', J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 33 (2018) 135–147. Unconditional: an infinite family of real quadratic fields with a two-element admissible set. Per Graves–Weiss 2025 (secondary, not verified): conditional on the Hardy–Littlewood conjecture and a 'Wieferich primes conjecture', every real quadratic field of class number one would be Euclidean. Not opened.
events.delivers: Unconditional family of fields with admissible primes, for Euclidean questions. Its link to the Wieferich question is through a hypothesis that is not stated in the sources read, so its relation to this bullet is unclear.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. It does not establish infinitude or finiteness of Wieferich primes.

Per Wikipedia's Wieferich prime article, the result is that any third base-2 Wieferich prime must exceed 2^64 (about 1.8 × 10^19). The PrimeGrid forum and project status pages were not opened.

events.what_happened: X. Caruso, Q. Gazda and A. Lucas, 'Wieferich primes for Drinfeld modules', arXiv:2412.11588 (v1 16 Dec 2024). Function-field setting: a main result links whether a monic irreducible polynomial is Wieferich to the valuation of special L-values of Drinfeld modules at that polynomial, extending Thakur's Carlitz-module result. They also study statistics and state that a place of degree d is Wieferich with probability q^(−d) when averaging over large sets of Drinfeld modules.
events.delivers: Function-field (Drinfeld-module) result on Wieferich places; a probabilistic heuristic for their distribution. Not integer Wieferich primes.
events.remains: All of problem_asks; no bearing on the integer question. The probabilistic statement is a heuristic, not a proof of infinitude.
events.doubts: Heuristic averaging result; not presented as a theorem about integer Wieferich primes.
events.direction: Neighbouring function-field result. Not on this bullet.

events.what_happened: H. Graves and B. Weiss, 'The abc conjecture implies infinitely many non-Wieferich places for fixed bases in number fields', arXiv:2503.19144 (v1 24 Mar 2025). Assuming abc: number-field analogues of the Graves–Murty and Ding results. Ding's result holds for all bases in imaginary quadratic rings of integers except for 31 listed exceptions. The abstract does not state an unconditional result and does not say whether the integer-base question is open. The integer-base Wieferich question is not addressed in the abstract.
events.revisions: v1 24 Mar 2025 only, per arXiv page
events.delivers: Conditional on abc for number fields: infinitely many non-Wieferich places for fixed bases in imaginary quadratic rings (minus 31 exceptions). Complementary side in number fields. Does not bear on infinitude of base-a Wieferich primes over Z.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The integer case is not addressed.
events.doubts: Conditional on abc for number fields. Full text not read; the 31 exceptions were not listed in the abstract.

events.what_happened: N. Fellini and M. R. Murty, 'Wieferich primes in number fields and the conjectures of Ankeny–Artin–Chowla and Mordell', arXiv:2508.08472 (v1 11 Aug 2025; v2 11 Feb 2026, 'final version'). Shows the AAC conjecture fails exactly when ε^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod 𝔭² (unconditional, number-field statement). Assuming Masser's abc for number fields, infinitely many prime ideals 𝔭 with α^(N𝔭−1) ≢ 1 mod 𝔭² for non-root-of-unity α. Also under finiteness of base-α super-Wieferich primes together with infinitude of base-α non-Wieferich primes. Lower bound of order log x / log log x. Secondary search summaries say it is in the Journal of Number Theory (2026), not verified on the journal page.
events.revisions: v1 11 Aug 2025; v2 11 Feb 2026 (listed as the final version, 17 pages); journal publication reported in 2026 by secondary sources only
events.delivers: Number-field analogues: the unconditional AAC equivalence (not an integer Wieferich statement), and conditional infinitude of non-Wieferich prime ideals. Restricted to number fields and to conditional hypotheses. Nothing unconditional on the integer Wieferich set.
events.remains: All of problem_asks over Z. The integer Wieferich infinitude question and the integer non-Wieferich question are both left open by this paper.
events.doubts: Conditional results on non-Wieferich prime ideals. A secondary search summary reports that the paper's introduction says there is currently no unconditional result in this direction; the abstract was not read as saying so. The journal publication was not verified.
events.direction: Number-field analogues; conditional infinitude of non-Wieferich prime ideals; unconditional AAC equivalence. Does not cut toward either answer for the integer Wieferich question.

events.what_happened: A. Lucas, 'Wieferich and Mersenne primes for function fields', arXiv:2512.08060 (v1 8 Dec 2025). Studies Wieferich primes for Drinfeld modules, their relation to Fermat equations and their finiteness or non-finiteness, and introduces Mersenne numbers for Drinfeld modules. The abstract states no theorem and does not say which direction the finiteness question goes. A search summary of a secondary review said it argues for non-finiteness in the function-field setting, using the function-field abc theorem; this was not confirmed in the abstract.
events.delivers: Function-field (Drinfeld) setting. Per the abstract only: studies the finiteness question; no theorem stated in the abstract. Not integer Wieferich primes.
events.remains: All of problem_asks over Z.
events.doubts: The direction of the finiteness claim conflicts between the abstract (silent) and the secondary summary (non-finiteness). Full text not read.
events.direction: Function-field setting; direction of finiteness claim not established from the abstract.

events.what_happened: L. Jones, 'Wieferich Primes and Monogenic Trinomials', arXiv:2605.13460 (v1 13 May 2026; v2 22 May 2026). Main theorem: F_p(x) = x^(2p) + 2x^p + 2 is monogenic if and only if p is not a base-2 Wieferich prime. The Wieferich condition is an input, not the object studied. The paper does not address whether there are infinitely many Wieferich primes.
events.delivers: Monogenicity criterion for one trinomial family, phrased in terms of base-2 Wieferich primes. Does not establish or move the count of Wieferich primes.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Uses the Wieferich condition as an input. Silent on infinitude.

events.what_happened: D. N. Giraudin, 'A counterexample to a conjecture of Thakur on Carlitz-Wieferich primes', arXiv:2607.15305 (v1 14 Jul 2026; v2 22 Jul 2026). Setting: F_q[T] with the Carlitz module, c-Wieferich primes to base 1, not integer primes. Thakur's 2015 conjecture (in odd characteristic every c-Wieferich prime has degree divisible by p) is shown false by an explicit irreducible c-Wieferich prime of degree 5 over F_{19^3}, since 19 does not divide 5. The paper states degree 5 is minimal and deferred the minimality proof and search method to a companion paper. v2 changed former Theorem 4.2 from an exactness statement to a conjecture; the counterexample is unchanged. The author reports an independent Magma check by D. Thakur.
events.revisions: v1 14 Jul 2026; v2 22 Jul 2026 (former Theorem 4.2 changed to a conjecture; counterexample unchanged)
events.delivers: Within function fields F_q[T] only: a degree-5 counterexample to Thakur's degree-divisibility conjecture for c-Wieferich primes. Restricted to the Carlitz setting over F_{19^3}. Says nothing about integer primes or the integer bullet.
events.remains: All of problem_asks over Z; this result is about function fields.

events.what_happened: A. Falk, J. Harrington and L. Jones, 'Generalized Wieferich primes and monogenic trinomials', arXiv:2607.29329 (v1 31 Jul 2026). Defines a prime p ≥ 3 as a base-b Wieferich prime when b^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p² for an integer b ≥ 2 (b = 2 is the classical case). Generalises the earlier monogenicity criterion to trinomials x^(2n) + bx^n + b for n ≥ 3 under restrictions on b. The abstract does not address whether there are infinitely many Wieferich primes.

events.what_happened: L. Jones, 'Generalized Wieferich primes and monogenic polynomials', arXiv:2609.13904 (v1 12 Sep 2026). Defines a prime p ≥ 3 as a generalized Wieferich prime base b when b^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p² (b ≥ 2). Gives necessary and sufficient monogenicity conditions for another trinomial class avoiding the Lucas-sequence condition, and extends them to N-nomials for N ≥ 4. Silent on infinitude.

events.what_happened: R. Laniewski, 'Radical defects, Wieferich primes, and the abc conjecture', arXiv:2609.00039 (v1 29 Aug 2026, math.GM). Studies coprime triples a + b = c through a radical excess and a defect. For the Mersenne family, the defect law involves Wieferich primes dividing 2^m − 1. An abc counterexample along the Mersenne line would require infinitely many Wieferich primes with exponential defect growth. A conditional observation; the paper does not claim to resolve the Wieferich question.
events.delivers: Conditional on abc: a necessary structural feature of a hypothetical counterexample along the Mersenne line. It does not prove or disprove infinitude of Wieferich primes.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: Single author with no affiliation on the arXiv page; category math.GM. Not a reason to doubt in itself, recorded for the judging pass.
events.direction: Conditional observation; infinitude of Wieferich primes appears only as a hypothesis for a counterexample. Does not cut either way on the bullet.

events.what_happened: G. Guedes and R. Machado, 'Perfect numbers, Wieferich primes and the solutions of C(2n,n) ≡ 2^n mod n', arXiv:2609.03091 (v1 2 Sep 2026). Abstract: solutions of the congruence C(2n,n) ≡ 2^n mod n are studied, the number of known solutions is improved using SageMath, and even perfect numbers and Wieferich primes are said to be connected to solutions. A secondary search summary says n = p² solves it exactly when p is Wieferich; this was not visible in the abstract.

disputes.summary: Carella (arXiv 1712.08166, v2 May 2018) states an unconditional density-1 result for non-Wieferich primes. Graves–Weiss 2025 and Fellini–Murty 2025 (as read in their introductions via secondary summaries) say no unconditional result of this kind is known. Not resolved; the Carella body was not read. Even if the density claim holds, it concerns non-Wieferich primes and does not settle infinitude of Wieferich primes.

The log x growth bound is attributed to Ding by Graves–Weiss 2025 and by Fellini–Murty 2025 (secondary summary), while Anitha et al. 2021 is not checked for attribution.

MathWorld's abc conjecture entry states that abc implies at least C ln x Wieferich primes ≤ x. Silverman (1988) and every other source found give the abc consequence as at least C log x non-Wieferich primes. The MathWorld wording appears to swap Wieferich and non-Wieferich. Reported from a search summary; the MathWorld page itself was not opened.

The statement given to this run reads a^p − 1 ≡ 1 (mod p²). The live Wikipedia bullet (fetched 2026) reads a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p²) with footnote [185]. The two readings agree at a = 2 and disagree at a = 1: the literal form has no solutions at a = 1, while the p−1 form holds for every prime. Which wording was frozen on 26 January 2024 was not verified.
Guedes–Machado arXiv 2609.03091 shows a 2026 submission date but a journal reference of 2023 (Notes on Number Theory and Discrete Mathematics 29). Not resolved.

Lucas arXiv 2512.08060: the abstract is silent on the direction of its finiteness claim, while a secondary review summary says it argues for non-finiteness in the function-field setting. Not resolved; neighbour only.

summary: The bullet asks whether, for each integer a > 0, infinitely many primes satisfy the congruence in its statement. I read the statement as given (a^p − 1 ≡ 1 mod p²) and also the Wikipedia live wording (a^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p², footnote [185]), because the two differ. They agree at a = 2 and differ at a = 1: the literal form has no solutions there, the p−1 form holds for every prime. The Wikipedia Wieferich prime article still lists the base-2 question as open 'as of 2026', with only 1093 and 3511 known; the article states the question for base 2 only, and gives PrimeGrid's 2022 bound of 2^64 and Dorais–Klyve's 2011 bound of 6.7 × 10^15. No source found proves or disproves the infinitude of base-a Wieferich primes for any a, conditionally or not. The conditional results all concern the complementary set of non-Wieferich primes: Silverman 1988 under abc, Graves–Murty 2013, Chen–Ding 2017, Ding 2019 (order log x under abc), Kotyada–Muthukrishnan 2016 and Graves–Weiss 2025 for number fields, and Anitha et al. 2021 for Lucas sequences. Fellini–Murty 2025 (v2 Feb 2026) gives conditional number-field analogues and an unconditional number-field AAC equivalence, not an integer result. Close calls: (i) Carella's 2017/2018 abstract claims an unconditional density-1 result for non-Wieferich primes, which conflicts with 2025 papers saying no such result is known; I did not read its body. Even if true, density 1 for non-Wieferich primes does not decide infinitude of Wieferich primes, so I treat it as off-scope. (ii) Several 2026 preprints (Jones, Falk–Harrington–Jones, Jones 2609.13904, Laniewski, Guedes–Machado) use the Wieferich condition as an input or connect it to other congruences and are silent on infinitude; I record them as discounted events. (iii) Caruso–Gazda–Lucas (Dec 2024) and Lucas (Dec 2025) are function-field results; the Lucas direction is unclear from the abstract. (iv) The Giraudin 2026 counterexample is to Thakur's conjecture for Carlitz c-Wieferich primes over F_q[T], not integer primes; I record it as a discounted neighbour. AI: no event on this bullet credits an AI system. The only AI-credited Wieferich-adjacent work is Giraudin, whose Section 6 names 'Claude Opus 4.8, Anthropic'; the Breakthrough Tracker says no AI role was disclosed, which conflicts with the paper and is recorded as a dispute. Searches combining Wieferich with Claude, GPT, GPT-5, OpenAI, DeepMind, AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, Gemini Deep Think, Lean, and Erdős-problem AI tracking found no AI-credited result on this bullet. The Erdős AI contributions wiki has no Wieferich entry. Sra's 'GPT, the Counterexample Machine' (Aug 2026) names GPT Pro but does not mention Wieferich primes. Two unrelated 2026 AI prime-gap reports (a GPT-5.6 claim via secondary aggregators; Axiom's 246 theorem) were noted and not pursued as they concern prime gaps. The heuristic that base-a Wieferich primes are infinite but sparse (roughly 1/p probability per prime, log log x count) is widely stated (Crandall–Dilcher–Pomerance; Caruso et al.; Laniewski) and is a heuristic, not a proof. Source limits: most in-window papers were read through abstract pages; full texts were not read except the Giraudin HTML methodology section. The pre-2024 journal papers were not opened and are recorded from secondary summaries.
competing_reading: One could read the Fellini–Murty and Graves–Weiss growth results as moving a quantity the bullet names, because they grow a count of 'non-Wieferich places' or 'prime ideals' for base α. That reading does not hold for the bullet as stated: the bullet asks for infinitely many primes where the congruence HOLDS, and these results count primes where it FAILS. A second reading takes the literal a^p − 1 ≡ 1 wording at face value, so that a = 1 is a finite instance (zero primes), which makes the universal claim false as written. The Wikipedia p−1 reading makes a = 1 trivially true. A third reading treats the 2017/2018 Carella density-1 claim as bearing on the bullet; it concerns the complementary set and so does not decide infinitude of the Wieferich set, unless the claim were misread as density-positive for Wieferich primes.
what_would_settle_it: For the question as written: a proof, in the literature or on arXiv, that infinitely many primes p satisfy a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p²) for a given base a (or a disproof for some a), or the same for the literal a^p ≡ 2 (mod p²) form. For the wording: the January 2024 frozen Wikipedia revision and footnote [185]. For Carella: the body of arXiv 1712.08166 and any later paper citing its density-1 claim. For AI: the full text of 2607.15305 (the author's explicit account already quoted; the tracker's contrary statement would be settled by the paper itself) and any future authors' statement of AI use on a Wieferich paper. For the older journal papers: Silverman 1988, Graves–Murty 2013 and Chen–Ding 2017 full texts, to confirm the exact growth statements and whether any unconditional step exists.

judgement.why: No event touches the infinitude of primes satisfying the congruence over Z for any base. The abc-conditional growth results (Silverman, Graves–Murty, Chen–Ding, Ding, and the number-field/Lucas analogues) all count the complementary non-Wieferich set, so they answer a changed question: variant. Dorais–Klyve and PrimeGrid are finite searches: instances. Function-field work (Caruso–Gazda–Lucas, Lucas, Giraudin) is an analogue: variant; Giraudin's object is a counterexample to Thakur's function-field conjecture, not to this statement, so object_role null. The monogenicity, abc-defect and binomial-congruence papers use the Wieferich condition as an input: none. Giraudin's AI role is answered as assisted from the paper's own account that the assistant designed and ran all the computations that produced the counterexample; the event is a variant either way, so this does not affect the problem. Guedes–Machado gets after_snapshot null because the record shows a 2026 arXiv date against a 2023 journal reference.
judgement.doubts: The given statement (a^p − 1 ≡ 1 mod p²) differs from the standard a^(p−1) form, and at a = 1 the literal form has no solutions. Nothing in the record moves either reading. The Giraudin AI basis_quote is thin by itself; the assisted call rests on the researcher's summary of the methodology section.
